producer_report.summary:
I added `athena approve-work <id>` and `athena reject-work <id> --why "..."`. They decide a steward proposal (a work item of kind `proposal`) by its id. The root cause of the blind reading was that the old request only cited the work item by a `records/` reference, which readers cannot see. Approving now builds a request from the work item itself. It carries the title, rung, key, queue time and role. The source and each cited reference are copied in as text: a job's request, reading and outcome; a file's text; a directory's file list; or a commit's message. The request is then read through the usual `ask`.

The decision is recorded as a new append-only record, `athena.work-decision/1`, at `records/work-decisions/<YYYY-MM>/<id>.json`. It holds the work item's id and either the approving job or the rejection reason. An item with a decision is no longer open. A second decision, an unknown id, a work item that is not a proposal, and an empty reason are all refused. An id can also be given as the work item's record path.

`athena status` lists open proposals with their ids and gains `approve-work` and `reject-work` lines under `next`. The README, CHANGELOG and `roles-and-ladder.md` are updated.

New tests cover the record's round trip and validation, the pure decision logic, and five CLI tests (`work_decisions.rs`). The CLI tests cover the status listing, approval with inlined content and a linked job, rejection, the refusals, and the two commands' `--help`. `cargo test --locked`, `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` all pass."

checks_run.note: Run as `cargo test --locked --quiet`; every suite passed, none failed. Ignored tests were already ignored.

open_issues: The deliverables list named crates/athena-gate/src/records.rs, crates/athena-cli/src/steward tests (crates/athena-cli/tests/steward.rs) and crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs as modify, but I left all three unchanged. The gate needed no change, and I judged the steward and its tests did not need one either. Say so if you wanted edits there.

The approved request can be long. It includes up to 6,000 characters per cited file and per job request, and up to 60 listed paths per directory. There is no total cap, and `ask` applies no length limit.
A cited path that exists only in the steward's workspace (for example GIT-LOG.txt) or a non-file name such as `github` is described as not in the repository. Its content cannot be inlined.
A steward proposal is not recorded as having been carried out. The decision record links the item to the job, but nothing follows the job through to landing.
docs/design/requirements-map.md was not touched; no requirement row is claimed.
mistakes: I first tried `git grep` and a piped `tail`. The hooks denied both, and I switched to the Grep tool and `--quiet` output.
I dumped far more of records.rs and steward.rs into context than I needed, which cost budget.
learnings: The steward's work items cite evidence by reference only (job id, path or commit), and a steward 'path' can be a directory (records/jobs), a workspace-only file (GIT-LOG.txt) or a bare name (github). The inlining has to handle all of these.

The `AnyRecord` envelope needs a new variant, a canonical path, a schema string and a validation arm to add a record type. athena-gate loads records through `AnyRecord::parse`, so it needed no change.
`Records::has_record_id` did not cover work items. I added work items and work decisions to it so a new decision id cannot collide.
The producer's Bash blocks `tail` and `grep`, and the Grep tool cannot read outside the working directory. Use `cargo test --quiet` for compact output.
desires: A way to read a tool-result file that Bash output spilled to outside the working directory, so a long `cargo test` log can be searched.
